prerequisites: CS-UH 1052 and CS-UH 2010 (no corequisites) — required, exam-tested prior coursework, not optional background
courseDescription: A required, cumulative 3-credit systems course covering operating system design from process/thread management through memory and file systems, textbook Silberschatz/Galvin/Gagne 'Operating System Concepts' (10th ed.). Every enrolled student is examined on the full syllabus; there is no elective/alternative-track content.
assessmentMethods: Homework assignments 5% (ongoing), 4 programming projects 35% (weeks 6, 9, 12, 15, done in pairs), midterm exam 20% (week 8, covers Ch.1-5), final exam 40% (week 17, cumulative). 60% of the grade is exam-based on material every student must know.
learningObjectives: Produce OS-development solutions using systems programming techniques
Apply systems APIs to build OS modules (processes, threads, synchronization primitives)
Model core OS concepts (scheduling, memory management, deadlocks) analytically
Apply theory-taught tools to practical systems problems
Experimentally evaluate OS design tradeoffs (scheduling policies, page replacement, I/O performance)

blocks.title: OS Foundations & System Structure
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — every pathway must cover this regardless of prior systems-programming background; students with no prior OS/C exposure get extra scaffolding nodes here.
objectives: Define the role and services of an operating system
Describe classic OS structures (monolithic, layered, microkernel)
Distinguish user mode from kernel mode operation

blocks.title: Processes & Inter-Process Communication
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — process abstraction is foundational to every later block.
objectives: Describe the process lifecycle and process control block
Compare shared-memory and message-passing IPC mechanisms

blocks.title: Threads & CPU Scheduling
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block; includes a midterm-review assessment checkpoint (material through this block is on the week-8 midterm).
objectives: Compare threading models and threading libraries
Apply CPU scheduling criteria and evaluate scheduling algorithms

blocks.title: Process Synchronization
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — synchronization primitives are tested on the final and used in Project deliveries.
objectives: Apply mutexes, semaphores, and monitors to the critical-section problem
Analyze classic synchronization examples (producer-consumer, dining philosophers)

lessons.title: Process Synchronization: The Critical Section Problem

blocks.title: Deadlocks
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block — smaller than others by lesson count, floor should scale down proportionally, not disappear.
objectives: Apply deadlock prevention, avoidance, and detection strategies

blocks.title: Memory Management (Physical & Virtual)
blocks.pathwayNote: Required floor block, heavily project-relevant (memory management project deliveries).
objectives: Compare contiguous allocation, paging, and segmentation
Apply virtual memory concepts: demand paging, page replacement, thrashing

blocks.title: I/O Systems & File Storage
blocks.pathwayNote: Required capstone block — final exam is cumulative, includes a final-review assessment checkpoint.
objectives: Describe I/O interfaces and subsystem performance
